title: TP-00 - Theophysics Blue Sheet
claim: Theophysics should be introduced as a fair comparison between competing explanatory frameworks using the same observations and standards, asking which explains more with fewer independent assumptions while remaining coherent.
assumptions: Competing frameworks can be compared by coherence, explanatory power, assumption cost, register honesty, reach, failure visibility, and human fit.
Theophysics must not be granted theological shortcuts when making physics-side claims.
Closed naturalism must count its own primitives and hidden subsidies.
definitions: Hidden upgrade: promoting a claim into a stronger register than evidence supports.
Hidden subsidy: relying on a primitive such as truth, lawfulness, or intelligibility without counting it as a cost.
negative_guards: Do not say physics proves God.
Do not let theology rescue weak physics.
Do not let naturalism use truth, lawfulness, or moral obligation without counting assumption cost.
kill_conditions: If the comparison applies stricter standards to one framework than the other, the blue-sheet rule fails.
If Theophysics hides bridge-status limits, the document must be revised.
If naturalism's assumptions are criticized unfairly or inaccurately, the comparison must be corrected.
